name: Whole-Book Bible Study
description: Read an entire biblical book, trace its structure and message, and apply its teaching.

sections.title: Read the whole book
sections.guidance: Read the book through, preferably more than once and in more than one translation. Note first impressions, recurring words, tone, genre and questions before consulting commentaries.

sections.title: Author, audience and setting
sections.guidance: Investigate authorship, recipients, historical and geographical context, occasion and purpose. Separate statements in the book from scholarly proposals and unresolved questions.

sections.title: Overview and central concerns
sections.guidance: Record main people, events, themes, key verses and the book's broad movement. Avoid treating every recurring word as the main theme.

sections.title: Structure and content
sections.guidance: Divide the book into natural literary units with passage references and brief headings. Explain how each section contributes to the whole.

sections.title: Message and development
sections.guidance: Trace the narrative or argument across sections, attending to genre, contrasts, promises, commands and how the conclusion relates to the opening.

sections.title: Central message
sections.guidance: State the book's subject, what it teaches about that subject, and its overall message, supported by the text.

sections.title: Application
sections.guidance: Consider implications for belief, worship and life that follow from the book's message and its place in the whole Bible.

sections.title: Further study
sections.guidance: List difficult passages, historical questions, relevant cross-references and sources to revisit.
